stories.notes: analyze_root_cause() correlates a reported Issue against already-computed STORY-005/013 signals (demand anomalies, supplier delays, supplier reliability scores) deterministically - no LLM/ML call. RootCauseAuditStore/RootCauseEvaluator mirror supplier_evaluation's STORY-013 trust-spine pattern exactly. RootCauseAnalysisAgent plugs into the existing Orchestrator and derives signals from raw rows the same way RiskDetectionAgent/SupplierEvaluationAgent already do. Demo proven against both synthetic data and a real local Postgres instance (scripts/local_test_db.py, from STORY-005).

criteria.text: Given a scenario input, when the system simulates it, then it should provide impact assessments.
Given invalid scenario parameters, when the system attempts simulation, then it should notify the user of errors.

stories.notes: simulate_scenario() applies caller deltas (demand %, lead time, safety stock, stock) to a baseline InventoryPosition and re-runs STORY-004's assess_stockout_risk() on both baseline and projected positions, reporting the diff as the impact assessment - no new risk model invented. ScenarioSimulationAuditStore/ScenarioEvaluator mirror root_cause's STORY-007 trust-spine pattern, with input_parameters persisted on every record (AC3 requires the actual inputs, not just confidence). ScenarioSimulationAgent plugs into the existing Orchestrator and reuses inventory_risk/data_quality.py to validate the raw baseline row before simulating, separating data-processing errors from invalid-scenario-parameter errors. Pre-commit /code-review high found and fixed 3 real input-validation bugs in the agent (non-dict baseline_row, non-string scenario_name, explicit-null delta field each crashing instead of returning a clean error response) - see PROGRESS.md for detail.

stories.notes: analyze_shipment_delays() reuses risk_detection/anomaly_detection.py's detect_supplier_delays() for all per-row validation and delay detection - no second delay-classification implementation. Cost analysis is a logged assumption (not escalated, same posture as reliability.py's own delay-threshold default): no delivery row in this codebase carries a real transportation-cost field yet, so delay cost is a flat DEFAULT_COST_PER_DAY_LATE=$150/day rate, with an optional per-row transportation_cost layered underneath as a base cost when a caller has real freight data. Delays are grouped into per-supplier SupplierDelayPattern (AC1). An unusable transportation_cost value is flagged in cost_errors and treated as $0 rather than raising (the 'cost calculation errors' failure path). ShipmentDelayAuditStore/ShipmentDelayEvaluator mirror supplier_evaluation's STORY-013 trust-spine pattern exactly (idempotent JSONL store, run-level record when zero delays are found, crash_error surfaced instead of an unhandled exception) - satisfies AC3. ShipmentDelayAnalysisAgent plugs into the existing Orchestrator/RecommendationAgent pipeline; unlike SupplierEvaluationAgent, a run with zero delayed POs is reported status="ok" (every delivery on time is a real, successful finding), not an error. Demo script (run_sample_shipment_delay_analysis.py) run live: exit code 0, 3 delays grouped into one SlowFreight pattern, $4,350 total cost, 3 audit records confirmed written.

criteria.text: Given data inputs, When quality checks are performed, Then the system provides a Data Quality Score
Given poor data quality, When detected, Then the system alerts the data steward
Trust: Given data quality monitoring, Then an audit trail of quality checks is maintained

stories.notes: assess_data_quality() is deliberately domain-agnostic (parameterized by required_fields) rather than a third hand-rolled, single-dataset validator alongside inventory_risk/data_quality.py and risk_detection/anomaly_detection.py's own delivery-row checks, which already own their domain's business rules and are not duplicated here. Scores a completeness dimension (missing-vs-falsy field distinction reused from those two modules' own convention) into a 0-100 Data Quality Score, higher-is-better (opposite polarity from this repo's risk scores) - satisfies AC1. A score below the 'fair' bucket floor (70/100), or zero rows to assess at all, raises poor_quality with alert_reasons rather than fabricating a number (the 'Incorrect Data Quality Score' failure path). QualityAuditStore/DataQualityEvaluator mirror supplier_evaluation's and shipment_delay_analysis's own trust-spine pattern exactly (idempotent JSONL store keyed on (check_id, dimension), crash_error surfaced instead of an unhandled exception) - satisfies AC3/Trust. Alerting the data steward (AC2) is a logged assumption, not escalated: no notification service is wired up for this project yet (same situation every other *Evaluator here is in), so the alert is a distinct, loudly logged data_quality_alert_raised event plus a run-level audit record (dimension=None) persisting the alert reasons, for a future notification service to consume. Demo script (run_sample_data_quality_monitoring.py) run live: exit code 0 - synthetic_good_quality scores 100/100 with no alert, synthetic_poor_quality scores 25/100 with an audited alert, real_data (no PostgreSQL credentials configured) alerts on zero rows rather than crashing or fabricating a score. Post-commit alignment fix (user asked for a review against the other stories before closing this one out): every other analysis story (STORY-003/004/005/013/014) has a dedicated agents/*_agent.py wrapper plugged into recommendation/run_sample_recommendation_demo.py's stage-1 pipeline, so its findings reach RecommendationAgent; STORY-015 initially had none, leaving the steward alert log/audit-trail-only. Added DataQualityMonitoringAgent, wired into that same stage-1 list. No contract change: AgentFinding.subject_kind is a closed Literal["sku","po","period","supplier"] in agents/contracts.py that a whole-batch completeness check doesn't fit, so this agent reports via recommendation+confidence only (findings=[], same shape DemandForecastingAgent uses) rather than extending that enum. Unlike its siblings, zero delivery_rows is reported status="ok" here (the zero-data alert IS the finding), which changes what the real_data demo scenario now demonstrates in a no-credentials environment - the module docstring was updated to say so, and the "no successful agent output" failure path it used to illustrate live remains independently covered by agents/tests/test_recommendation_agent.py and recommendation/tests/test_synthesis.py.
